title: Deadlines that feel kind
description: A deadline can be a helpful fence or a daily threat. The difference is in how you set it and what happens when life moves it.

body.heading: What deadlines are actually for
paragraphs: A good deadline answers one question: when will I decide this is done or review how it is going? It protects a project from drifting forever and protects your other plans from the project.
Trouble starts when a self-set estimate becomes a moral verdict. Missing a guessed date is information about the guess, not a character flaw.

body.heading: Set them soft, then review honestly
paragraphs: When you set a deadline, add the reason and a review point: 'Draft by Friday so I can rest the weekend; check progress Wednesday.' If the date slips, move it once, consciously, and note why.
For shared work, kindness also means honesty early. Telling someone on Tuesday that Friday is impossible is far kinder than silence followed by a missed Friday.

takeaway: Use deadlines as fences and review points, not as verdicts on your worth.
